original_question: For operator scaling, does there exist a quantum analogue of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, or any divergence at all, such that the operator Sinkhorn algorithm can be written as an alternating minimization procedure?
target_in_paper: Section 4 (Takeru MATSUDA): the open problem asking whether the operator Sinkhorn algorithm for operator scaling admits a divergence-based characterization analogous to the classical Sinkhorn algorithm’s Kullback-Leibler-divergence characterization for matrix scaling.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct open problem very closely. It correctly singles out operator scaling/operator Sinkhorn, asks for a quantum analogue of the Kullback-Leibler divergence or more generally some divergence, and asks whether the algorithm can be expressed as an alternating minimization procedure. That is exactly the issue raised in Section 4.
missing_details: The paper is specifically about the operator Sinkhorn algorithm for operator scaling, not operator scaling in a broader or unrelated sense.

The classical comparison point should be stated explicitly: for matrix scaling, the Sinkhorn algorithm is described as alternating e-projections and as alternating minimization of the Kullback-Leibler divergence.
The official formulation is slightly broader than a quantum KL analogue: it asks whether there exists some divergence at all, with a quantum KL analogue mentioned only as the natural first candidate.
The nearby context in the paper says that the operator Sinkhorn algorithm has already been interpreted as alternating e-projections with respect to the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) metric.
The paper highlights the obstruction that the space of density matrices has non-vanishing torsion; this is part of the reason the divergence formulation remains open.

To make the question fully stand-alone, it should say that the desired divergence should reproduce the operator Sinkhorn algorithm itself as the alternating minimization procedure, i.e. give the same kind of characterization as in the classical matrix-scaling case.

Section 4 does not introduce additional algebraic restrictions such as ambient field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers; those notions are inapplicable here and should not be added.
refined_question: For the non-commutative matrix-scaling problem of operator scaling, does there exist a divergence on the space of density matrices—ideally a quantum analogue of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, but more generally any divergence at all—such that Gurvits’s operator Sinkhorn algorithm is exactly realized as an alternating minimization procedure, in the same sense that the classical Sinkhorn algorithm for matrix scaling is alternating minimization of the Kullback-Leibler divergence?
justification: Section 4 is the exact target of your draft: it first recalls the classical KL-divergence characterization of matrix Sinkhorn, then introduces operator scaling as the quantum/non-commutative analogue, and finally states that, although the operator Sinkhorn algorithm is known to be alternating e-projections with respect to the SLD metric, it remains open whether it can be written as alternating minimization of some divergence because of non-vanishing torsion on the space of density matrices. I therefore kept your question narrow, retained the classical-to-quantum comparison that motivates the problem, named the exact algorithm, and avoided adding technical hypotheses not present in the paper’s formulation.
